tl.text: This is VOID. Give an AI agent real on-chain power, with a guarantee it can never leave your rules. A smart contract checks every action.
tl.cap: Real on-chain power for an AI agent. Enforced by the contract.

tl.text: Every action passes five gates, in a fixed order: expiry, spend cap, whitelist, transaction count, rate limit.
Let's build a vault. I set the owner, and the one contract and function the agent may call, then seal the policy on-chain. Live, on Base Sepolia.
Sealed. Five gates armed. I fund it, and take the session key, shown once.
Now I'm the agent. Outside the policy, simulated: blocked at the whitelist. Now for real.
Reverted on-chain. The chain itself refused it.
Same key, doing what the policy allows. It goes straight through. No human in the loop.
If anything looks wrong, one owner signature pulls the plug.
Now every action is blocked at the first gate.
And what is left sweeps straight back to the owner.

One more test. That was me. So I told a real AI agent it was hijacked, and to drain a vault. It tried the whole balance, sneaking under the cap, a token transfer, even uninstalling the policy. Five attempts, five rejections. The one approved action went through.
tl.cap: A real AI agent, told to rob it

tl.text: Real ERC-4337, twenty-eight Foundry tests, live on Base and Arbitrum. VOID: session keys for agents that the contract itself enforces.
tl.cap: Session keys for agents that the contract itself enforces.
